root.name: Slav Defense: Slav Gambit, Alekhine Attack
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nc3 dxc4 4. e4

overview: White plays 4.e4 instead of retaking c4, building a big centre and offering the pawn. The main reply 4...b5 supports the extra pawn, and White continues 5.a4 to attack the b5 pawn, with a queenside fight and open lines for development. Black can keep the pawn but must be careful with the king and the weakened queenside.

white_ideas.idea: 5.a4 to undermine b5, then Nf3 and Bxc4 or Bd2 with a lead in development.
Use the e4-d4 centre and open lines to attack before Black consolidates.

black_ideas.idea: Hold the c4 pawn with ...b5 and ...Bb7 or ...e6.
Return the pawn at the right moment to complete development.

typical_structures.structure: White centre pawns e4 and d4 against Black's b5/c4 advanced pawns and c6.

character.notes: Pawn down for White, open lines and forcing play after 4...b5 5.a4; both kings can be exposed.

gambit.notes: Black can try to hold c4 with ...b5; White has no forced regain.

soundness.notes: Played by strong players occasionally; thought roughly sound with compensation, not refuted.

structure.notes: Centre opens as e4 and d4 meet c-pawn and pieces; lines open early.

approach.notes: Less common sideline but strong players do play it; still standard.

level.notes: Needs specific forcing lines after 4...b5 5.a4 to know the right moves.

sublines_that_differ.name: Quiet 4...e6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black returns the pawn early; no gambit, calm play.

character.reason: Open lines, a pawn down for White and forcing play after 4...b5 5.a4.

gambit.reason: White offers c4 and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: Compensation is real and the line is still played by strong players.

structure.reason: Game turns on open lines for pieces after e4 against the c4 pawn.

approach.reason: Rare but played by strong players, not a surprise-only line.

level.reason: Forcing queenside lines must be known precisely.

plans.reason: White trades a pawn for time and a broad centre.
